answer.rationale: Finance mandate requires an 18% cut and the incumbent has explicitly refused to reopen price this cycle, ruling out negotiate_terms and renew_incumbent as viable paths to the cost target. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate outright. Memory_c2 records a prior successful switch to a low-cost vendor with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, which supports feasibility, but that record is from a different sourcing cycle and component context, so it needs archive verification before being trusted as directly applicable. Memory_c1 (incumbent renewal stability) is checked as a counterfactual to confirm how much continuity value would be forfeited by switching, since the line is at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer and any transition hiccup could breach delivery commitments. Given the 14-day contract expiration forces a decision now, I lean toward switching but at a standard (not broad) rollout scale to limit exposure while the new vendor ramps, rather than assuming c2's smooth onboarding will repeat exactly. Downstream value risk is flagged because a cost-driven switch under a zero-buffer production constraint could increase delivery risk even if unit cost drops, which conflicts with the stated objective of not increasing delivery risk.
